rules.description: A like-for-like light bulb replacement is usually low risk if no wiring, fitting repair, or unsafe height access is involved.
rules.warning: Turn the light switch off, let the bulb cool, and use stable access if the fitting is overhead.

rules.description: Electrical wiring, exposed wires, breakers, outlets, switches, fixtures, and ceiling fans can create shock or fire risk.
rules.warning: Switch off power at the breaker and verify the circuit with a voltage tester before touching any wiring.

rules.description: Main panel, service panel, breaker panel, and meter work expose users to high-current electrical hazards.
rules.warning: Do not open or modify the main electrical panel unless you are licensed and authorized.

rules.description: Electrical work near water has elevated shock and code-compliance risk.
rules.warning: Electrical work in wet areas needs GFCI/RCD protection and should be checked by a licensed electrician.

rules.description: Small accessible leaks may be manageable if water can be isolated, but hidden pipe damage can escalate quickly.
rules.warning: Shut off the water supply before disassembly and keep the area away from live electrical points.

rules.description: Burst pipes, flooding, and leaks near electrical points can damage structures and create electrical hazards.
rules.warning: Shut off the water supply and avoid electrical switches, outlets, and appliances near water.

rules.description: Water heater work can involve pressure, temperature, gas, and electrical hazards.
rules.warning: Water heater repairs should be handled by a qualified plumber or technician.

rules.description: Wall demolition can involve structure, hidden utilities, dust, debris handling, and permit requirements.
rules.warning: Confirm the wall is non-load-bearing and scan for hidden electrical, plumbing, or gas services before demolition.

rules.description: Concrete, brick, and masonry cutting creates dust, flying debris, vibration, and tool-control risk.
rules.warning: Use eye, respiratory, hand, and hearing protection when drilling, cutting, or breaking masonry.

rules.description: Tiling needs surface preparation, cutting control, waterproofing awareness, and curing time.
rules.warning: Check surface flatness, waterproofing needs, and tile-cutting PPE before starting.

rules.description: Wet-area tiling can fail if waterproofing, slope, drain details, or sealing are incorrect.
rules.warning: Wet-area tiling needs correct waterproofing and drainage details to avoid leaks and mold.

rules.description: Interior painting is usually low risk when ventilation, ladder safety, and surface preparation are controlled.
rules.warning: Ventilate the room, protect surfaces, and use a stable ladder for edges or ceilings.

rules.description: Painting at height or disturbing old paint can add fall, dust, and lead-paint exposure risk.
rules.warning: Do not sand suspected lead paint without proper containment and respiratory protection.

rules.description: Light shelves and simple assembly are usually manageable if the right fasteners and wall type are known.
rules.warning: Check wall type and avoid drilling before scanning for hidden wiring or plumbing.

rules.description: Heavy cabinets, doors, railings, and overhead fixtures can fail if not anchored into suitable structure.
rules.warning: Heavy mounted items should be fixed into suitable structure using rated fasteners.

rules.description: Filter replacement and simple thermostat battery changes are usually low risk if power and model compatibility are checked.
rules.warning: Turn the HVAC system off before opening covers or replacing filters.

rules.description: Refrigerant, compressor, furnace, duct, and AC unit work may involve pressure, electricity, combustion, or regulated materials.
rules.warning: Use a licensed HVAC technician for refrigerant, compressor, furnace, or hardwired AC work.

rules.description: Gas line work can cause fire, explosion, poisoning, or code violations.
rules.warning: Leave the area and contact emergency services or a licensed gas technician if a gas leak is suspected.

rules.description: Load-bearing walls, beams, foundations, and support columns require structural assessment.
rules.warning: Do not alter structural elements without approval from a qualified structural engineer.

rules.description: Roof repair adds fall risk and weather exposure.
rules.warning: Avoid roof work without proper access, dry conditions, and fall protection.
